title: Qué vs. cuál/cuáles

text.text: Spanish has two main interrogative pronouns for asking «what» or «which»:
asks for a definition, category, or open description — it invites the speaker to identify or explain something from scratch.

asks for a selection from a known or implied set — it invites the speaker to pick one (or more) from existing options. The choice between them depends on the communicative function of the question, not on whether the English equivalent is «what» or «which».

children.text: Use qué to ask for a definition or category.

text.text: When the question asks «what is X?» and expects an explanation or classification, use qué. This applies especially with the verb ser and abstract nouns.

children.text: Use qué directly before a noun.

text.text: In standard European Spanish, qué functions as an adjective and precedes a noun directly: ¿qué libro?, ¿qué color?, ¿qué día? Cuál/cuáles cannot fill this slot.

children.text: Use cuál/cuáles to select from a set.

text.text: When a group of options is present or implied and the question asks the listener to choose, use cuál (singular) or cuáles (plural). It is typically followed by de + a noun phrase or used as a standalone pronoun.
Spanish does not strand prepositions at the end of a question. Any required preposition moves to the front, immediately before the interrogative word: ¿con quién?, ¿a qué hora?, ¿adónde?
When asking about a destination (movement towards a place), use adónde rather than dónde.
The interrogative words themselves do not conjugate, but cuál has a plural form. The table below summarises the forms and their typical syntactic position.

text.text: All interrogative words carry a written accent (tilde) when used in direct or indirect questions: qué, cuál, cuáles, quién, dónde, adónde, cómo, cuándo.

note.text: Qué + ser asks for a definition of an abstract concept. Cuál would be wrong here.

body.en: Which of these two do you prefer?

note.text: Cuál selects from an explicit set (estos dos). Note cuál is followed by de, not placed directly before a noun.
Qué acts as an adjective directly before the noun libro. Cuál cannot occupy this position in standard European Spanish.

body.en: Who are you going to the cinema with?

note.text: The preposition con moves to the front of the question, immediately before the interrogative quién.

body.en: Where are we going this summer?

note.text: Adónde (not dónde) is used because the verb ir expresses movement towards a destination.
